items.name: Frame rails and outriggers
items.guidance: Probe with a screwdriver at welds and anywhere that holds standing water. Surface scale is fine; flaking layers or a screwdriver that sinks in is not.

items.name: Tongue / A-frame junction
items.guidance: Cracks at the welds where the tongue meets the main rails. Known failure point on these.

items.name: Coupler
items.guidance: Latch wear, play in the ball socket, pin and clip present.

items.name: Safety chain attachment
items.guidance: Welded loops intact and not rusted thin.

items.name: Torsion axle condition
items.guidance: Trailing arms should sit level or slightly up. Pointing down and rearward means the rubber has sagged.

items.name: Wheel camber
items.guidance: Tires tilting inward at the top point to a worn or sagged axle.

items.name: Leaf springs (if equipped)
items.guidance: Flattened arch, broken leaves, worn shackle bushings.

items.name: Wheel bearings
items.guidance: Jack each wheel, spin it, feel for grit. Rock at 12 and 6 o'clock for play.

items.name: Grease seals
items.guidance: Grease weeping onto the backing plate or the inside of the wheel.

items.name: Tires — DOT date code
items.guidance: Four-digit code on the sidewall, week and year. Over 6–7 years old means replace regardless of tread.

items.name: Spare tire and jack
items.guidance: Present, correct size, holds air.

items.name: Body-to-frame bolts
items.guidance: Rusted through, missing, or holes elongated from movement.

items.name: Brakes (if equipped)
items.guidance: Drum condition, magnet wear, adjuster function.

items.name: Breakaway switch and battery
items.guidance: Cable intact, switch functional, battery holds charge.

items.name: Tongue jack and stabilizers
items.guidance: Crank freely, no bent legs, footpads present.

items.name: Harness to tow vehicle
items.guidance: Connector corrosion, chafed insulation along the tongue.

items.name: Belly band seam — exterior
items.guidance: Press along the full perimeter. Loose or missing rivets, gaps, failed sealant.

items.name: Belly band seam — interior
items.guidance: Staining, damp insulation, or rust tracks below the seam line inside.

items.name: Window frames — all corners
items.guidance: Corners are where they leak. Look for staining below each corner inside.

items.name: Window glazing seals
items.guidance: Cracked or hardened rubber, fogged panes.

items.name: Window weep holes
items.guidance: Clear and draining. Blocked weeps push water inward.

items.name: Window frame availability
items.guidance: Note make and model. Original parts are scarce — this decides repair vs. replace.

items.name: Roof vent
items.guidance: The most common leak on the trailer. Lens for UV cracking, flange for sealant failure.

items.name: Door frame seal and gasket
items.guidance: Compression all the way around, no daylight, gasket not flattened.

items.name: Door sag and latch alignment
items.guidance: A door you have to lift to latch suggests shell or floor movement.

items.name: Running and marker light flanges
items.guidance: Sealant condition at every lens.

items.name: License plate light
items.guidance: Small penetration, routinely overlooked.

items.name: City water inlet
items.guidance: Sealant and backing condition.

items.name: Propane line pass-through
items.guidance: Grommet or sealant intact where the line enters.

items.name: Appliance vents
items.guidance: Fridge and furnace flange sealant, screens intact, no nesting.

items.name: Interior ceiling corners
items.guidance: Brown staining is the tell-tale. Note exactly where — it points at the leak above.

items.name: Smell test
items.guidance: Musty or earthy means active or recent moisture.

items.name: Screw heads inside
items.guidance: Rust bleeding from a screw head means water is reaching it.

items.name: Full-floor walk
items.guidance: Cover every square foot on hands and knees. Press hard. Soft, spongy, or crunchy all mean rot.

items.name: Door threshold
items.guidance: Highest-probability rot location on the whole trailer.

items.name: Under the dinette
items.guidance: Hidden by furniture, so almost never inspected.

items.name: Wheel well areas
items.guidance: Road spray plus any wheel well seam failure.

items.name: Perimeter where floor meets shell
items.guidance: Separation, gaps, or a lip that has lifted.

items.name: Underside probe
items.guidance: From below, probe the plywood with an awl wherever you can reach. Note thickness and whether it's sealed.

items.name: Floor-to-frame contact points
items.guidance: Rot concentrates where wet plywood sat on steel.

items.name: Stress cracks at window corners
items.guidance: Cracks radiating from openings. Note whether they go through or are gelcoat only.

items.name: Stress cracks at door corner
items.guidance: Same check, plus watch for flex when the door swings.

items.name: Cracks around through-hardware
items.guidance: Anywhere a bolt or screw passes through the shell.

items.name: Gelcoat buff test
items.guidance: Compound a small oxidized patch by hand. If gloss comes back, you may not need paint at all.

items.name: Crazing vs. structural cracking
items.guidance: Low angle in raking light. Fine spider webbing is cosmetic; a defined line you can catch a fingernail on is not.

items.name: Previous repairs
items.guidance: Mismatched patches, filler bridging cracks, abandoned holes from old hardware.

items.name: Delamination at the seam
items.guidance: Tap along the belly band. A dull thud instead of a sharp tick means separation.

items.name: Roof surface
items.guidance: Most UV-degraded panel on the trailer. Do not stand on it — the span is unsupported.

items.name: Which furniture is bonded to the shell
items.guidance: Dinette base, closet, and galley are often glassed in and carry load. Identify before removing anything.

items.name: Shell shape reference
items.guidance: Measure diagonals and width at several heights before gutting, so you can detect deformation later.

items.name: Bracing plan
items.guidance: If structural furniture comes out, decide now what temporarily braces the shell.

items.name: Insulation behind panels
items.guidance: Wet, compressed, or missing.

items.name: Original items worth keeping
items.guidance: Some original fixtures carry real value. Photograph and set aside before demo.

items.name: Converter
items.guidance: Original units are usually dead or unsafe. Assume replacement.

items.name: 12V fuse panel and grounds
items.guidance: Corrosion, loose lugs, undersized or missing grounds.

items.name: Wire insulation
items.guidance: Brittle, cracked, or sun-baked insulation anywhere in the runs.

items.name: DIY splices and taps
items.guidance: Twisted-and-taped joints, wire nuts, house wire. All get replaced.

items.name: Shore power cord
items.guidance: Jacket condition, ground pin present and intact.

items.name: Battery box and venting
items.guidance: Secure mounting, vented if lead acid, condition of the tray.

items.name: Battery disconnect
items.guidance: Present and functional.

items.name: Running and brake lights
items.guidance: Test every function with the tow vehicle connected.

items.name: Interior lighting circuits
items.guidance: Function, and note what you plan to keep.

items.name: Planned new loads
items.guidance: List every future load now — it drives wire gauge and panel sizing at rough-in.

items.name: Tank date and OPD valve
items.guidance: Recertification required every 10 years. OPD (triangular handle) valve required to refill.

items.name: Regulator age
items.guidance: 10–15 year service life. Replace if the age is unknown.

items.name: Hard lines and flex hoses
items.guidance: Cracking, chafing at pass-throughs, corrosion at fittings.

items.name: Manometer leak test
items.guidance: Full system pressure test. Soapy water alone won't find a slow leak.

items.name: Stove burners
items.guidance: Light evenly, blue flame, valves not seized.

items.name: Furnace (if present)
items.guidance: Ignition, blower, condition of the combustion air path.

items.name: Absorption fridge
items.guidance: Often a straight swap to 12V compressor. Yellow residue on the cooling unit means ammonia leak.

items.name: Propane detector
items.guidance: These expire. Check the date.

items.name: CO detector
items.guidance: Also expires. Check the date.

items.name: Fresh water tank
items.guidance: Cracks, off smell, secure mounting, condition of the fill line.

items.name: Supply lines
items.guidance: Old grey poly with crimp fittings should be replaced on sight.

items.name: Freeze damage
items.guidance: Split fittings and cracked valves from a missed winterization.

items.name: Water pump or hand pump
items.guidance: Function, mounting, and noise.

items.name: Sink and drain routing
items.guidance: Trap present, drain path, grey water handling.

items.name: Water heater (if present)
items.guidance: Anode condition, tank condition, bypass valves.

items.name: VIN plate
items.guidance: Legible and matching the title. A missing plate is a real registration problem.

items.name: Title status
items.guidance: Clean title in hand, matching the VIN.

items.name: GVWR vs. planned build
items.guidance: 13-footers have very little payload. Budget cabinetry, battery, water, and gear before designing.

items.name: Current scale weight
items.guidance: Weigh it as-is if you can, so you know your starting point.

items.name: Tongue weight
items.guidance: Should land around 10–15% of total. Decides where heavy items can go.

items.name: Photo documentation
items.guidance: Photograph everything, including wiring and propane routing, before any demolition.
